clue.text: She scans a novel for an Englishman

indicators.note: novel means new or unusual, so the letters of the preceding words take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A woman reads a novel looking for a particular Englishman in its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book she scans, but it is the anagram signal on SHE SCANS A. The answer is the Scots (and Gaelic) word for an English person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is a Scottish, often mocking, term for a person from England.

clue.text: Desire for public transport?

definitions.meaning: the tram in Tennessee Williams's play, whose title names it Desire
a tram running on rails in a city street, in American usage

explanation.surface: Is longing a reason for taking the bus?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desire' looks like longing, but it is the name of the tram in Tennessee Williams's play A Streetcar Named Desire.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Orleans tram line called Desire gave a famous play its title, and a city tram is a form of public transit.

clue.text: Shoe thus worn by serviceman on square

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed on top of, so the square comes below
worn by means the word for thus is put on like clothing around the serviceman

parts.note: so means thus
AB is an able seaman, a serviceman
a T-square is a draughtsman's square, so T

explanation.surface: A sailor on the parade ground is wearing the right shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, a type of footwear.

clue.text: Go abroad, finally settling in a Muslim territory

indicators.note: in puts the last letter of settling inside the territory

parts.note: an emirate is the domain of an emir, a Muslim ruler

indicators.note: finally picks only the last letter of settling

explanation.surface: To move abroad, at last making a home in an Islamic state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settling' looks like part of the surface's emigrant making a home, but only its last letter is used. 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle in another.

clue.text: Classical writer's impressive article

parts.note: august means grand and impressive
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An ancient author's essay is magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': a classical writer is an Augustan.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of the age of the emperor Augustus, or of the English neoclassical period, are given this label.

clue.text: Who, surprisingly, had erected a high seat?

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters of who come out in an unexpected order
erected means set upright, so in a down clue had reads upwards

explanation.surface: Someone asks, astonished, who put up a tall chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' scrambles WHO to HOW, and 'erected' turns HAD upward to DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is a canopied seat carried on an elephant's back.

clue.text: Possibly man's attempt to limit exercises

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in, so the word for attempt is placed around the exercises

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A man makes an effort to cut down on his workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': possibly man is a two-legged animal. 'Possibly' marks man as one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A biped is any two-legged creature, and a human being is one example.

clue.text: Sent an account for being sick and out of action?

indicators.note: being here means existing within, so the word for sick is placed in the bed

parts.note: someone out of action is laid up in bed
ill means sick

explanation.surface: An invoice arrives because the worker was off sick and laid up.
explanation.walkthrough: The container is implied by the sense: someone sick and out of action is ill in bed, so the sick word sits in the bed. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be billed is to be sent an invoice, a statement of what is owed.

clue.text: One demonstrating in favour of old currency

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a tester was an old English silver coin of the Tudor period

explanation.surface: A marcher who backs a return to an old monetary system.
explanation.walkthrough: A TESTER was a Tudor shilling, later a sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: A protester takes part in a demonstration against or for a cause.

clue.text: Line up the ensemble?

definitions.meaning: military sense: troops ... ranks, aligning themselves
an outfit of clothes worn together

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the order in which a musical group is arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers dress their ranks by straightening them, and a woman's frock can be a whole outfit.

clue.text: Making fun of a form of needlework?

definitions.meaning: teasing someone in a good-natured way
in knitting, raised alternating vertical ridges of plain and purl stitches

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether teasing could count as a kind of sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing is called this in slang, and knitters use the same word for ridged stitching on cuffs.

clue.text: Gladly accepted the Spanish firm in western state

indicators.note: in places the Spanish article and the company abbreviation inside the letters for western and the state

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, a US state
el is Spanish for the
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A Spanish company was warmly received in a western American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western state' looks like one place, but it gives two pieces, W and ME, with ELCO set between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A welcome guest or offer is one received with pleasure.

clue.text: Persian queen loses husband in the compound

indicators.note: loses means the queen's name is left without the letter for husband

parts.note: Esther was the Jewish queen of the Persian king Ahasuerus in the Bible

explanation.surface: A Persian queen is widowed inside the royal compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a walled enclosure for the queen, but it is the chemist's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an ester is an organic compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Bogus student invades quarters, being unprincipled

parts.note: a sham is something bogus or fake

indicators.note: invades means the student letter forces its way into the letters for quarters

parts.note: compass quarters: two easts and two souths, E, E, S and S
L is the learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A fake student breaks into lodgings, behaving without scruple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings, but it stands for compass points; L goes between the first two to give ELESS after SHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without shame or scruple is lacking in moral principles.

clue.text: Woman quietly takes in point of this nonsense

indicators.note: takes in means the woman and quiet letters enclose the abbreviation for point

parts.note: Clara is a woman's name
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A woman softly makes her point about the rubbish being talked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is the abbreviation pt, not a sharp tip. 'of this' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk, rubbish meant to win applause.

clue.text: .Plant that's found in a posh bar? It could be

indicators.note: found in means the abbreviation for that is sits inside the rearranged letters

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

indicators.note: could be means the letters of a posh bar it may be rearranged

parts.note: ie (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A flower might turn up in a smart bar, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges U, BAR and IT into UBRTIA, and 'found in' puts the abbreviation for 'that is' inside it. The dot before the clue is a stray printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubrietia is a low trailing rock-garden flower with purple blooms.

clue.text: Moderate Tories rejected this course

indicators.note: rejected means the word for moderate Tories is sent back, read from the end

parts.note: wets was Margaret Thatcher's name for moderate members of her Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Centrist Conservatives turned down a particular policy direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a political line, but it is a dish in a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew is a dish served as one part of a meal.

clue.text: Wicked ways ended when Grundy was married

indicators.note: wicked suggests twisted or crooked, so the letters of ways ended are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A man's sinful habits stopped once he wed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Solomon Grundy was born on a Monday, christened on Tuesday and married on Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, Solomon Grundy wed on the third day of the week.

clue.text: Sullen type starts scolding pet belonging to us

indicators.note: starts picks only the first letter of scolding

parts.note: our means belonging to us
puss is a pet cat

explanation.surface: A grumpy person begins telling off our cat.
explanation.walkthrough: S comes first, then OUR and PUSS: the charade runs in the answer's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A sourpuss is a bad-tempered, sulky person.

clue.text: God is besieged by prayer far too much

indicators.note: is besieged by means the god's name is surrounded by the word for prayer

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request, a prayer
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A god is overwhelmed by too many prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or overabundance.

clue.text: Note about former pupil's vestment

indicators.note: about means the note goes around the letters for a former pupil

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
OB is an old boy, a former pupil of a school; the 's joins

explanation.surface: A note concerning an old pupil's ceremonial dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long flowing garment, and a vestment is such a ceremonial gown.

clue.text: Caught like some doves

definitions.meaning: seized or arrested, as by the scruff of the neck
the ... dove has a black ring round its neck

explanation.surface: A remark that a pair of doves was captured.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab someone by the neck is to seize them, and one dove species has a ring of dark neck feathers.

clue.text: Sound heard when we're in love with these beauties?

definitions.text: Sound heard when we're in love with these beauties?

parts.words: Sound heard when we're in love with these beauties?
parts.note: lovers are said to hear wedding chimes ringing, and the word for that chiming sounds like the word for pretty women

explanation.surface: A romantic wonders what ringing they hear when smitten with lovely women.
explanation.walkthrough: Wedding bells are said to ring for lovers; BELLES sounds just like them and means beautiful women.
explanation.definitionFit: Belles are beautiful women, and the word is said like the chimes rung at weddings.

clue.text: Old council abandoning caution and formality

indicators.note: abandoning means the word for caution is dropped from the council's name

parts.note: the Star Chamber was an old English court of the king's councillors
amber is the traffic light that signals caution

explanation.surface: A historic council threw caution aside and stood on ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star Chamber was a Tudor court notorious for arbitrary rulings; amber is the caution light on British traffic signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch means stiffness or formality of manner.

clue.text: Spear found outside church in the Midlands

indicators.note: found outside means the spear goes around the letters for church

parts.note: a leister is a pronged fish-spear
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An ancient spear is dug up outside a Midlands church.
explanation.walkthrough: A LEISTER is a three-pronged spear for catching fish. LEICESTER is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a county town in the East Midlands region of England.

clue.text: Ball hit high through porch

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high in tennis or cricket
by can mean through, by means of

explanation.surface: A ball is lofted through an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is an entrance hall or vestibule, like a porch.

clue.text: Volunteers set out to try a tiny portion

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: out means the letters of set are put out of order

explanation.surface: Volunteers start out to sample a little of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' reads as one verb, but 'out' is the anagram signal on SET, giving STE.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to sample a very small amount of it.

clue.text: Council makes unknown contribution in lecturers' rise

indicators.note: contribution in means the unknown letter is put into the reversed word
rise in a down clue means the word reads upwards, from the end

parts.note: dons are university lecturers
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A council makes an unknown donation towards the university lecturers' pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns DONS to SNOD and 'contribution in' puts Y after the S. 'makes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church officials, a church council.

clue.text: Striker without money is involved in a struggle

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the striker surrounds the money

parts.note: a batter strikes the ball in baseball or cricket
L is the pound sign, the abbreviation for money in pounds

explanation.surface: A penniless batsman is caught up in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: L sits inside BATTER. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A battler is a fighter, one engaged in combat or a hard fight.

clue.text: Belonging to nobody? It's not conceded

definitions.meaning: to own up is to admit or concede, so this is not admitted

explanation.surface: A thing without an owner is said to be something nobody will admit.
explanation.definitionFit: Property with no possessor lacks an owner, and a fact nobody has admitted is not owned in the sense of confessed.

clue.text: Poet still without a son

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so still goes around the a

parts.note: yet can mean still, as in still more

explanation.surface: A poet is still without a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means outside: A sits inside YET, and S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Save the line by careful management

parts.note: to husband resources is to save or conserve them
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Careful management will rescue the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like rescue, but it is husband in its sense of to conserve. 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is economical management of resources, as well as farming.
